title: NGS-based deep bisulfite sequencing
author: Lee, Kim

steps.title: Combine and normalize PCR products
steps.instruction: Combine all PCR products amplified from bisulfite‑converted DNA and normalize the DNA amount of each individual product.

steps.title: End‑repair reaction
steps.instruction: Prepare the end‑repair mix: add X µl of the combined PCR product, 5 µl End repair enzyme mix, 10 µl 10× End repair reaction buffer, and add H₂O to a final volume of 100 µl.

substeps.instruction: Incubate at 20 °C for 30 min in a thermocycler.

steps.title: First size selection on agarose gel
steps.instruction: Prepare a 2 % agarose gel, load the entire 100 µl end‑repair reaction into one or two wells, and load a 100‑bp size marker in a separate well.

substeps.instruction: Run the gel at 100 V for 40 min.

steps.title: Gel extraction of desired fragments
steps.instruction: Excise the gel region containing the PCR products of the desired size range and extract DNA using the Zymoclean Gel DNA Recovery Kit.

substeps.instruction: Elute the purified DNA in 20 µl TE buffer.

steps.title: Adapter ligation reaction
steps.instruction: Set up the ligation mix (total 40 µl): 17 µl size‑selected DNA, 1 µl Bst 2.0 warm polymerase (8000 U ml⁻¹), 4 µl Bst 2.0 polymerase buffer (10×), 4 µl T4 DNA ligase (400 000 U ml⁻¹), 4 µl T4 DNA ligase buffer (10×), and 10 µl P1 + A Barcode Adapter (10 pmol µl⁻¹).

substeps.instruction: Incubate at 25 °C for 25 min, then at 65 °C for 30 min, and finally at 80 °C for 20 min to stop the reaction.

steps.title: Second size selection
steps.instruction: Repeat the 2 % agarose gel size‑selection procedure (steps 3–4) on the ligation product.

substeps.instruction: Elute the DNA in 10 µl distilled water.

steps.title: PCR amplification of library
steps.instruction: Amplify the eluted DNA with the following primers: P1 adapter primer (5′‑CCACTACGCCTCCGCTTTCCTCT‑3′) and A adapter primer (5′‑CCATCTCATCCCTGCGTGTCTCC‑3′).

substeps.instruction: PCR program: 95 °C 5 min; 10–14 cycles of 95 °C 30 s, 68 °C 30 s, 72 °C 45 s; final extension 72 °C 10 min.

steps.title: Cleanup of PCR product
steps.instruction: Purify the final PCR product using the DNA Clean & Concentrator Kit.

steps.title: Final size selection
steps.instruction: Perform size selection of the purified library fragment using the E‑Gel Precast Agarose Electrophoresis system.

steps.title: Final cleanup of library fragment
steps.instruction: Clean up the size‑selected DNA library fragment again with the DNA Clean & Concentrator Kit.

steps.title: NGS sequencing
steps.instruction: Submit the prepared library for next‑generation sequencing on the chosen platform.

steps.title: Pre‑process raw NGS reads
steps.instruction: Using the supplied Perl scripts, (1) remove reads shorter than 100 bp and sort reads into files per PCR product with test_sam_3.pl (producing two files per product, one for each primer).

steps.title: Merge per‑product read files
steps.instruction: Combine the two files belonging to the same PCR product with the Perl script test_merge.pl.

steps.title: Run BiQ Analyzer HT
steps.instruction: Create a TSV file (with test_tsv.pl) that lists the absolute paths to (a) the original unconverted fasta files for each PCR product and (b) the sorted bisulfite read files, then execute BiQ Analyzer HT via test_biq.pl.

steps.title: Extract methylation metrics
steps.instruction: Extract the number of reads used, % methylation, and standard deviation from the BiQ Analyzer HT output using the Perl script test_extract.pl.

steps.title: Compile results for analysis
steps.instruction: Import the final text file containing DNA methylation levels for all PCR products into Excel (or similar) for downstream calculations and inspection.

description: So far, we have performed three independent trials of DNA methylation analyses using this protocol [6]. These test trials have successfully derived the DNA methylation levels of on average 80% of individual PCR products. While performing these trials, however, we have come across a couple of technical issues, which may be responsible for the observed failure, the remaining 20% of the PCR products. First, the initial DNA amounts of some of these PCR products were lower than those of the other PCR products. As a consequence, the sequence reads from these products were not as well represented as the other products in the final sequencing output. It is, therefore, very important to normalize the initial DNA amounts of individual PCR products at the early stage of library construction (Step 1 in Fig. 1A). Also, it is advisable to perform an independent protocol, such as COBRA (Combined Bisulfite Restriction Analysis) [7], before the actual bisulfite sequencing given the possibility that PCR could enrich one type of DNA sequences, such as unmethylated DNA compared to methylated DNA. Second, the size of some of sequence reads turned out to be much smaller than their predicted sizes based on the initial sizes of PCR products. According to detailed inspection, the sequences of these products were truncated at homopolymeric regions, such as poly A or T. These are typical sequences for bisulfite-converted DNA since many Cs are converted to Ts during the bisulfite conversion reaction. According to our recent study [6], similar polymeric repeats are often detected in mammalian genomes, 2 out of 12 amplified PCR products with the average length being around 300 bp in length. Although the exact cause for this truncation is currently unknown, one culprit might be the potential stalling and subsequent falloff of DNA polymerase from template DNA during the sequencing reaction of NGS. One remedy to this problem may be avoiding homopolymeric regions while selecting target regions. Also
